Trump says victory over Iran 'at hand', stress that Tehran will 'never have a nuclear weapon'
item.description:
Trump says victory over Iran 'at hand', stress that Tehran will 'never have a nuclear weapon'

US President Donald Trump said that Washington will be victorious over Iran "whenever" he wants it to happen. 

"We have victory at hand (in Iran). It's going to be whenever, sort of, whatever I want it to be. To be honest, and we're trying to be nice, we're giving them every chance to make a deal and save a lot of lives. But I am not sure if they are going to take advantage of that," he said during Thanksgiving calls with US service members.

Trump also praised US forces for their role in the war on Iran, adding that they would never allow Tehran to have nuclear arms. 

"Each of you is playing an essential role to protect not only our country today but future generations of Americans by ensuring that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon. They will never have a nuclear weapon. That I can tell you."

University of Michigan faculty vote in support of pro-Palestine students facing charges
item.description:
University of Michigan faculty vote in support of pro-Palestine students facing charges

Nearly 60 percent of voting faculty members at the University of Michigan have backed a resolution in support of a dozen former students and staff who are now facing federal criminal charges for their participation in the 2024 anti-war encampments for Gaza. 

The move is symbolic but also an indication of where much of the teaching staff stands. 

On 12 November, after 2,425 members of the Faculty Senate voted on a motion stating that the Department of Justice's indictment "is part of a broader attack on both Palestine solidarity and labor unions in the United States", results showed 58.2% expressed support. 

That's more than 1,000 professors, lecturers, clinicians, and other University of Michigan employees. 

Read more: University of Michigan faculty vote in support of pro-Palestine students facing charges

item.title: South Korea assures Iran that it has no plans of participating in the war
item.description:
South Korea assures Iran that it has no plans of participating in the war

During a phone call, South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun assured Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi that Seoul has "no intention of intervening in or participating in the war".

The two exchanged views on their bilateral relations and the situation in the Middle East, discussing recent diplomatic efforts and initiatives to maintain peace and stability in the region.

According to a post on X by the Iranian Embassy in Seoul, Araghchi expressed concern regarding the "presence of any foreign military forces in the region, stressing that rather than contributing to peace and security, such a presence would heighten tensions and expand the scope of the conflict".

"Foreign Minister Cho reaffirmed South Korea’s support for peace and stability in the region, assuring Foreign Minister Araghchi that South Korea has no intention of intervening in or participating in the war and no plans to deploy troops to the region," the post added.

item.title: Israeli police clash with Haredi protesters opposing mandatory military service in Jerusalem
item.description: Israeli police clashed with ultra-Orthodox Jewish protesters, known as Haredim, during a demonstration against mandatory military service at the Bar-Ilan Junction in West Jerusalem on Thursday, Anadolu Agency reports. Mounted police and officers moved in to disperse protesters attempting to block traffic, using force against demonstrators. Haredim make up about 13 per cent of Israel’s population of more than 10 million. They have traditionally refused military service, saying they need to devote themselves to studying the Torah and that integration into secular society threatens their religious identity. The dispute over Haredi military service has intensified as hundreds of reservists continue to be called up amid ongoing escalation on several fronts, including Gaza, Lebanon, Iran and the occupied West Bank. item.title: Iran says Qatari, Pakistani mediation in talks with US continues
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Thursday that mediation efforts by Qatar and Pakistan in negotiations between Tehran and Washington are continuing. Speaking to Iranian state television, Araghchi said Qatari and Pakistani mediators remain engaged and are regularly conveying ideas and proposals between the two sides. He said, however, that Iran’s Foreign Ministry is prioritizing efforts to strengthen the country’s economic resilience against sanctions rather than focusing solely on negotiations. Tehran is working through various channels to meet its needs and counter attempts to impose an economic blockade and sanctions, he added. “We are examining ideas that could open new paths, but we insist on implementing our demands related to reopening the Strait of Hormuz,” Araghchi said. item.title: ‘NAZA’ documentary on Gaza screened at UN office in Geneva
item.description: “NAZA,” a documentary exposing Israel’s killing of civilians in Gaza, was screened at the United Nations Office at Geneva on Thursday, Anadolu reports. The screening was organized by the Permanent Observer Mission of the State of Palestine to the United Nations Office. The film, produced by The Guardian, received widespread acclaim at the Venice Film Festival, drawing a 25-minute standing ovation before being awarded the Special Jury Prize. Abraham and Szor took the stage to accept the award, with Abraham speaking about a smear campaign against their film in Israel and efforts to prevent the facts presented in it from being seen. item.title: Iran denies attacking vital facility in Kuwait
item.description: Iran on Thursday denied attacking a vital facility in Kuwait, saying its armed forces had not conducted any military or offensive operations in the region, Iran’s Fars news agency reported. Senior Iranian Armed Forces spokesman Abolfazl Shekarchi “categorically and completely” rejected allegations by the Kuwaiti military that Iranian forces had targeted one of the country’s vital facilities. Shekarchi pointed to what he described as a “history of hostile actions” by Israel and US forces, accusing them of involvement in false-flag operations and regional adventurism.
